output.brief: The Kestria buffering is most likely caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not by the CDN move. In the 12–25 October data, smart-TV 5.2 users on Tessaline sit at about 5.9% rebuffering, while the same CDN serves the web player, mobile apps and smart-TV 5.1 (auto-update off) at about 0.6–0.7%, and every ISP is affected only on 5.2. Other markets are normal. The handball launch does not fit: its match nights were flat and the rise started before it. Confidence is moderate-to-good, since the comparison is an ad hoc query and I did not check the cancellation survey or the encoding change log. Next, I would ask Product to revert 5.2 adaptive-streaming settings in Kestria to the 5.1 behaviour and pause the wider 5.2 rollout. Hold off on the Tessaline SLA notice, fee withholding and traffic move, which would punish the vendor for a fault it does not appear to own. Keep the ops alert on, and treat the cancellation link and any refund offer as unproven until checked.
